header:
Date: 2026-03-28 / Time: 15:00 UTC / Duration: 46m / Meeting ID: ff-20260328-clb-01
Redwood attendees: Maya Chen (AE), Liam O'Connor (SE), Nina Park (Solutions Eng)
Customer attendees: Sara Patel (Head of Platform), Tom Reyes (Security Architect), Jules Becker (Engineering Manager), Priya Singh (IT Ops)
summary: Customer wanted end-to-end validation of SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning plus review of RBAC and least-privilege model. Key asks: support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML, SCIM bulk sync and provisioning attributes, audit log retention and delivery, KMS integration options, and per-environment role separation for least-privilege. Redwood to share SOC2 and RBAC examples and run a live SCIM test in a staging tenant.
topics: SAML SSO setup (SP vs IdP initiation)
SCIM provisioning: attribute mappings, bulk sync, deprovisioning
Encryption and KMS options for private deployments
transcript:
00:00:01 - Maya: All right hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I run the account. Quick roll call?
00:00:08 - Sara: Hey Maya, Sara here, head of platform at ClearBank.
00:00:11 - Tom: Tom Reyes, security architect.
00:00:13 - Jules: Jules Becker, Eng mgr.
00:00:15 - Priya: Priya, IT ops.
00:00:18 - Liam: Liam O'Connor, I'm the SE, I'll cover SSO and SCIM details and RBAC patterns.
00:00:25 - Maya: Cool, thanks. We built an agenda in the calendar but high level: SAML SSO flow, SCIM provisioning, RBAC/least-privilege, audit logs, KMS & data residency Qs. We'll leave time at the end for next steps.
00:00:37 - Sara: Sounds good. We're mostly trying to validate that we can meet enterprise controls: SSO via our Okta tenant, SCIM to push users and groups, strict RBAC so only certain teams can manage models, and retention of audit trails for 7 years ideally. Also encryption keys — we prefer customer-managed keys when we go private.
00:00:56 - Liam: Great. On SSO, Redwood supports SAML 2.0. We do both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows; the quickstart covers metadata exchange, assertion consumer service URL, and attributes. We default to email and name attributes but you can map any claim from Okta.
00:01:12 - Tom: Okta's team will send SAML metadata. A question: can you enforce mfa for console logins and API tokens? We require MFA for interactive logins but service-to-service tokens are handled differently.
00:01:24 - Nina: Short answer, yes. For hosted accounts we integrate with your IdP's session policies so MFA is enforced via Okta. For programmatic API keys we recommend issuing short-lived tokens; on Private we can integrate with your existing token broker or use our KMS integration to rotate keys.
00:01:40 - Jules: When you say integrate with IdP policies, do you do step-up auth for risky actions, like model deployments or role changes?
00:01:46 - Liam: We have role-based guardrails and you can require admin-only actions for specific roles. Step-up auth isn't yet a built-in enforced flow for every action in hosted mode, but we can implement approvals/workflow integrations via webhooks; in Private you can push the enforcement to your IdP. We'll note that as an item.
00:02:00 - Tom: Noted. SCIM — what's your support level? We need full lifecycle: create, update, deactivate, and group push. Also want to sync custom attributes like team_id and entitlements.
00:02:11 - Liam: We support SCIM 2.0 and group push. Provisioning supports bulk sync and delta sync. Standard attributes (userName, id, active, emails, name) map out of the box. For custom attributes we'll accept extension attributes in the JSON payload; we'll share an attribute map. We also support 'externalId' and custom 'entitlements' if you want to push role membership.
00:02:29 - Priya: For deprovisioning, do you honor soft-deactivate vs hard delete? We need immediate disable on termination.
:02:35 - Nina: We honor 'active': false as immediate disable. You can choose to also call delete for full purge. We also persist audit records of the change; deletion of user objects is a separate retention policy.
00:02:47 - Sara: Speaking of audit, what's exported? We need who, what, when, which model version, and request metadata including IP and region. Exports need to be S3-compatible for our SIEM.
00:02:59 - Liam: Audit logs include user identity, action type, timestamp, IP, request id, model id and version, response status. We can stream to AWS Kinesis or dump to an S3 bucket (encrypted) on a schedule, or push to your syslog via a forwarder. Retention is configurable per account; in hosted we default to 90 days but can archive longer on request — for enterprise we have add-on retention to meet regulatory windows.
00:03:21 - Tom: For 7-year retention we probably need Private or an export pipeline. Clarify encryption in transit and at rest? KMS options?
00:03:28 - Nina: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+/HTTPs. At rest in hosted we use provider-managed encryption; enterprise Private supports customer-managed keys (we integrate with AWS KMS and HSM options for on-prem). Keys can be rotated and we support envelope encryption. We'll send our KMS integration doc.
00:03:43 - Jules: Data residency: we need logs and model I/O to stay in eu-west-1 for some customers. Can Redwood pin regions?
00:03:50 - Maya: Yes, we support region pinning for both hosting and Dedicated. For Private you control the region entirely. We'll note which logs can be pinned; some global control plane metadata still flows through our control plane unless you choose Private with a local control plane.
00:04:05 - Tom: Control plane telemetry is sensitive — is there an option for a local control plane with Private?
00:04:09 - Nina: Yes, Private includes an option for a customer-managed control plane with no egress of metadata. That's our on-prem or VPC deployment. We'll share the architecture doc.
00:04:18 - Sara: Back to RBAC — we need role separation by environment (prod/staging), and a least-privilege model so platform engineers can't spin up workloads in prod without approval. How do roles map?
00:04:29 - Liam: We recommend a role model: platform-admin (full in staging, restricted in prod), security-audit (read-only across environments), app-developer (deploy/invoke but not manage infra), billing-admin (view usage). You can scope roles to org/team/environment. We support org-scoped roles and resource tags to enforce environment separation.
00:04:46 - Jules: Can roles be synchronized from groups in Okta via SCIM?
00:04:49 - Liam: Yes, groups map to roles. We can map an Okta group to a Redwood role in provisioning. For least privilege, we encourage mapping minimal groups and using attribute-based access if you need fine grain.
00:05:00 - Priya: Is there an approval workflow for granting elevated roles?
00:05:03 - Maya: We don't have a built-in approval UI today, but we integrate with existing ticketing or identity governance via webhooks and SCIM deprovisioning can be used as a safety valve. For Private customers we can discuss SSO-linked approval flows. We'll log that as a product gap.
00:05:20 - Tom: Audit log integrity — do you provide signed logs or append-only ledger for compliance?
00:05:25 - Liam: We provide tamper-evident logs for Private deployments via chained hashes and can sign audit exports. In hosted, we maintain retention and access controls; for attestation you can request exports and we can provide checksums. For highest assurance we'd recommend Private deployment.
00:05:42 - Sara: Good to know. SCIM test plan — we want to run a staged provisioning test: push users, update attributes, remove user, push group membership changes, verify RBAC enforcement. Can Redwood run that with our test Okta tenant?
00:05:55 - Nina: Absolutely. Typically we ask for an Okta test tenant and a staging Redwood org. We'll perform SP metadata exchange, configure SAML SSO in test, then enable SCIM provisioning in incremental mode and monitor logs. We'll share a runbook.
00:06:08 - Tom: On token lifetimes — what are default API key TTLs and can we integrate short-lived AWS-style credentials?
00:06:16 - Liam: Hosted API keys are long-lived by default but we offer short-lived tokens via our session API; for Private you can plug in your STS. We have rotating ephemeral tokens for some integrations; we'll share docs.
00:06:27 - Jules: Any rate limiting or throttles that would impact automation during bulk SCIM sync?
00:06:31 - Liam: We have rate limits on the management API; for large orgs we can temporarily raise limits during initial bulk syncs when coordinated. Delta syncs are low throughput.
00:06:40 - Sara: Do you maintain a history of role changes, who changed what and when? That's important for audits.
00:06:45 - Liam: Yes change history is part of the audit logs; we log before/after for role mappings and provide an API to query history. Exports include the actor, timestamp, and previous state.
00:06:56 - Tom: About SCIM attributes: we'll need group membership to map to project entitlements and also a custom attribute for data residency tag. Can you store arbitrary user metadata?
00:07:06 - Nina: Yes we store extension attributes; they're searchable and can be used in policy evaluation. We'll include examples in the attribute map.
00:07:13 - Maya: Quick check — any blockers from your side to proceed to a test?
00:07:18 - Sara: We'll need legal to sign the DPA but from a technical POV we can provide an Okta test tenant and service account. The DPA is in process, should be done EOD Friday.
00:07:27 - Tom: We'll send the IdP metadata and attribute requirements by next week.
00:07:31 - Maya: Great. Action items recap: Maya to share SOC2 and SAML/SCIM quickstart; Liam to share RBAC role examples; customer to provide IdP metadata and test tenant. Schedule live SCIM test once we have artifacts.
00:07:45 - Jules: One more question — SCIM provisioning rate for very large orgs, like 50k users, any caveats?
00:07:51 - Liam: For very large orgs we recommend initial bulk export and staged imports. We can support chunked syncs and commit windows; may require Dedicated support to avoid hitting shared API rate limits. We'll coordinate with infra team.
00:08:05 - Priya: Do you support SCIM push for group nesting? Our Okta groups are nested and we rely on inheritance.
00:08:12 - Liam: SCIM doesn't universally standardize nested groups; we can flatten membership during provisioning and support a 'memberOf' attribute mapping. We'll include patterns.
00:08:22 - Sara: Thanks everyone. Let's target the week of April 6 for the live test.
00:08:27 - Maya: Sounds good, we'll send invites after artifacts land. Thanks all.
00:08:31 - [meeting ends]
